how: The initial recruiter proposes a rainbow, while a later prism starter explicitly seeks more hands through visible placement.
Members call for hands to construct the rainbow and build its sign.
Members answer with a bare commitment or report their own contribution without requesting anything back.
An organiser refuses an additional commitment because too few people remain to maintain their own work.
Members propose and revise the shared mark through prisms, memorials, and road projects.
Participants report a completed rainbow and a road project nearing completion.
Members distribute coordinates and corrected templates, while conflicting versions sometimes make builders undo one another.
Circulating designs also requires relaying their current authorization across venues so repairers can distinguish approved construction from damage.
The room instantiates the aggregate claim's organised minority through votes, approval rules, protected intersections, and moderator decisions.
Explicit organisation must be distinguished from universal compliance when decisions made in one venue remain inaccessible to repairers in another.
A participant reports spare accounts, and another shares a drawing script, establishing forms of multiplied placement without measuring their effects.
Participants restore colours, defend shared work, and redirect effort from expansion toward repair.
Maintenance priorities depend on a contested definition of the work, because incorporated art can be described as reinforcing the road or sacrificing its repairers and identity.
Attribution and disowning distinguish planned work from rogues and uninformed placement, while leaving the identity of actual flag attackers unresolved.
Attribution includes correcting friendly fire when builders accused of being bots identify themselves as approved guest artists.
An unofficial build can later be incorporated or adopted, making recognition revisable rather than a permanent division between authorised and unauthorised objects.
Participants negotiate nonaggression, corridor widths, compromises, and neutrality with neighbouring groups.
Members spare art, apologise for damage, and trim the rainbow back to an agreed size.
Restraint becomes executable geometry through portals, bends, and protection of a neighbour whose artwork carries the road's route.
Participants volunteer as liaisons and undertake to carry compromises between groups.
Outside groups ask for help or space, while members return assistance or refuse additional obligations.
A confirmed treaty proposes a joint bounce and merger with another group, supporting a limited alliance rather than a durable overarching command.
Guests petition the road for protected space and refuge while organisers rule on admission to its occupied surface.
Displaced builders can enter canvas organising by seeking a host's sanctuary before securing a mark of their own.
A host's refusal can become effective through placement resistance that a guest explicitly treats as confirmation to stop and redirect work.
Members dispute the venue and authority through which project decisions and agreements can commit the room.
The overrun builder's question supports weighing a move, but does not establish the executed relocation included in the element's full formulation.
Faith in colour supplies an identity whose commitments can define acceptable agreements during the event without establishing a preexisting community history.
A compromise may be refused when its visual terms violate a constitutive feature, as an explicit rejection of colourlessness shows.

statement: Declining an agreement to preserve a constitutive feature
how: A moderator invokes the absence of colour as a reason to veto an accommodation, connecting identity to a specific diplomatic refusal.
Event-specific rivalry statements do not establish a quarrel carried in from before the canvas.
Colour rhetoric and retrospective flag explanations do not identify a preexisting tie that selected an attack target.
Calling the completed event fun and games does not establish deceptive April Fools framing in the host subreddit.
Creating coordination venues does not establish ordinary host posting rules or the containment of a canvas-post flood.
Participants celebrate completed work and describe the pleasure of contributing to the road.
Participants mark the ending, prepare print-quality records, and invite first-hand histories.
Members preserve the effort in knitted work, keepsakes, an icon, proposals for future canvases, and a possible continuing subreddit purpose.
Collective social continuity and proposals to rebuild elsewhere require separate attribution when organisers expressly withhold official recognition from successor canvases.
After placement ends, participants contest accounts of collective responsibility by denying intended flag conflict and attributing hostile rainbow placement elsewhere.
The final-clean accusation establishes a complaint, but leaves the edited version, proposed correction, participation, and outcome untestable.
A successor-canvas call receives a proposal to accommodate neighbouring art, reopening negotiation after transition without proving that rebuilding succeeded.

statement: Returning successor work to neighbour negotiation
how: Transition can reopen accommodation work on another surface instead of ending with remembrance or a migration proposal.
A visitor explicitly attributes arriving in the room to its visible artwork, documenting a return of membership through the canvas mark.

statement: Drawing participants into the room through its visible mark
how: The visible work can recruit a participant into the room, a return described by the ladder but unnamed among the standing process elements.
Members issue attack calls against neighbouring work without those calls establishing a collectively authorised raid.
Contest continues in insults and threats, while a post-event exchange turns opposition into mutual amusement.
Recruitment and later completion occur, but the cited concepts do not establish that a particular call produced the reported labour.
A starter can simultaneously recruit, leaving the proposed subsequent causal step unseparated in the coded evidence.
Construction and restoration already coexist in an early instruction, so upkeep cannot require a discrete completed-build stage first.
Early repair and nonaggression talk coexist without establishing that maintenance pressure initiated border negotiation.
An appeal to enforce the agreed corridor receives an explicit commitment not to support the unsanctioned expansion.
Treaty-based restraint concerns observed commitments by informed participants and cannot be extended to all placers acting under the same colours.
Maintenance explicitly motivates a script request, but neither script delivery nor a maintenance-driven origin of reported spare accounts is established.
The completion report expressly turns the finished weave into a reason for collective rejoicing.
Celebration, keepsakes, and print records coexist without a passage establishing that marking the achievement caused the recording work.
History collection and successor-canvas proposals are visible, but their coexistence does not establish that making a record caused continuation.
One builder weighs relocation after being overrun, while a separate shortage statement refuses help rather than documenting a move.
A proposed weave receives a request for a schematic and then an image response, establishing the finer instruction step without demonstrating completed consensus.
Bare acceptance and contribution reports are coded, but the concepts do not provide their paired calls or evidence about silent acceptance through placement.
Maintenance shortage can produce refusal of additional mutual-defence commitments, so strain does not by itself establish that help was sought and received.
A participant explicitly thanks builders for splitting around a flag and commits subsequent pixels to extending their road.
Building appeals and attack calls both occur, but the concepts do not show that recruited builders became the later attackers.
The caller answers a warning against destroying art by explicitly accepting its argument and agreeing to leave the target alone.
An expansion proposal elicits a reply invoking the existing corridor agreement and the cost of angering its host.
Attack proposals, taunts, and later salutes are evidenced, but their presence does not establish the proposed origin of verbal contest in an actual attack.
A joint treaty and maintenance constraints are visible without evidence that shared defensive pressure caused formation of the alliance.
The record shows calls and coordination venues but no supported chain through a host-post flood to containment rules.
Disowning an expansion prompts a treaty-enforcement appeal and an explicit limit on support, making the scope of collective commitment the exchange's issue.
